summary.headline: Ind-Swift Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 50.15% YoY to ₹234.89 crore, with operating EBITDA margin at 18.02% and PAT of ₹31.03 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue was ₹234.89 crore, up 50.15% YoY and 26.22% QoQ, with operating EBITDA of ₹42.33 crore (18.02% margin) and PAT of ₹31.03 crore (13.21% margin). H1 FY27 revenue reached ₹420.97 crore (up 35.79% YoY), with H1 EBITDA margin at 17.97%. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of more than 50% and a medium-term target of ₹1,500+ crore by FY30, but did not commit to a 20% full-year EBITDA margin, which management called an internal target. Several questions on constant-currency figures, detailed capex and FY28 guidance were deferred or left open.

financial_highlights.change: +50.15% YoY from ₹156.43 crore; +26.22% QoQ from ₹186.09 crore
4.95x YoY from ₹8.55 crore; +27.04% QoQ from ₹33.32 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Raw material expenses (% of revenue, Q2 FY27)

financial_highlights.value: Net debt-free, with robust cash and liquid reserves

segments.name: Own brands (export)
segments.commentary: 55.75% of quarterly sales and 69% of export sales; management cited ₹125 crore of export own-brand revenue in Q2 and 68% own-product mix within the CDMO-plus-own split. Growth is driven by direct marketing and field force expansion in GCC, Central Asia and Africa.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.99% of sales per the presentation; management cited approximately ₹65 crore of CDMO revenue in Q2 versus about ₹15 crore in Q1. Atorvastatin + Ezetimibe contributed about ₹58 crore in Q2 versus about ₹25 crore in Q1.

segments.name: Ethical division (domestic)
segments.commentary: 5.43% of sales, led by chronic, pediatric and gynecology therapies. Domestic contract manufacturing was stated at 5% with 39 repeat domestic clients.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of more than 50% reiterated; management said it is in a 'very comfortable position' to achieve it. No explicit FY27 rupee revenue target was given.
Internal full-year FY27 EBITDA target of 20% (called the minimum internal target); Q3 margin guided at 19-20%, and blended FY27 margin said to be 'more than 19%'.
Medium-term: 20-25% revenue CAGR to cross ₹1,500+ crore by FY30, with 200-300 bps EBITDA margin expansion. Management said it is too early to revise the FY30 vision.
FY28 guidance may be revised upward, per management, but no number was given. Management declined to comment on whether ₹1,200-1,250 crore is reachable by March 2028.
CDMO incremental revenue of ₹100-130 crore in FY27 and ₹200-220 crore over two years. Ibuprofen expected at about ₹20 crore in Q3 and ₹20-25 crore in Q4.
Over 330 additional product registrations expected in FY27; about 100-150 already secured in H1 per Shalika Malhotra.
Working capital requirement of about ₹350 crore at ₹1,500 crore turnover (FY30). Inventory target minimum 90 days; debtor target about 60 days.
capex_capacity: ₹250 crore growth capex (Samba EU-GMP upgrade, Derabassi warehouse, R&D infrastructure, debottlenecking) stated as fully on track; ₹45 crore for the Samba EU-GMP/PIC/S upgrade is on schedule.
Samba plant utilisation at 70-75%; Derabassi (100% EOU) utilisation at 70-75%.

Derabassi warehouse land acquired, construction started; warehouse shift expected in 10-12 months, freeing space for additional manufacturing. Management said Derabassi capacity is sufficient to reach ₹1,200 crore by FY28.
Samba: ANVISA (Brazil) visit expected probably in Q4 FY27; PIC/S/EU approval expected sometime in FY28.
Detailed capex timelines and asset turns to be shared separately via ConfideLeap, not on the call.
demand_pricing: Ibuprofen sachet (Viatris CDMO): about ₹15-16 crore revenue in H1 FY27; site variation approved and supplies under way. Management expects ₹20 crore in Q3 and ₹20-25 crore in Q4.
Clarithromycin dry suspension: commercial validation completed; European launch awaits customer variation approval, after which batches start. Site variation still awaited.
Macrogol sachet (Aerotex): product developed in-house and supplied.
Global registrations crossed 900+ across 85 countries, with 2,100+ dossiers filed. Management said 520 are own registrations and about 950 total.
Europe is about 47% of geographic export mix; management said Europe is stable and payment-oriented, so no reduction is planned.
NPPA revised price control list: no impact, as the portfolio falls outside it.
New-customer revenue of about ₹80-90 crore this year from newly acquired international customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance achievable given H1, and what about FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 guidance is comfortable. FY28 guidance may be revised up, but no figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹1,200-1,250 crore top line by March 2028 achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is very difficult to comment on March 2028 now and would update at the next call with FY27 numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 20% EBITDA margin hold for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 20% the minimum internal target for the team and said it will maintain that level in the next full year. For FY27, Q3 is guided at 19-20% and blended margin is above 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Synthimed stake monetisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Majority holder IndiaRF may sell some stake in coming quarters, and Ind-Swift has tag-along rights and may participate if valuations are good. Management sees ₹7,000-8,000 crore value for Synthimed and holds 7.80%.

qa_highlights.question: Sourcing of APIs and key starting materials?
qa_highlights.answer: Majority of key starting materials and APIs come from Synthimed. Total purchases are about ₹100 crore out of about ₹400 crore of raw material procurement this year. China imports are limited to one or two molecules.

qa_highlights.question: Pipeline and new molecule timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: There are 11 molecules due by FY28-FY29 and two more in FY29-FY30. Management said no new molecule is expected in FY28. Products are finished formulations, not APIs. Registrations start in early FY28; commercialisation late FY28 or FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Average realisation cycle is 75 days. Management expects receivables to fall in Q3 after a strong October collection period. Working capital need is about ₹350 crore at ₹1,500 crore turnover.

risks_watch: Revenue and margin ramp depends on Q3 and Q4 execution: 20% full-year EBITDA requires above 20% in H2 after Q1 and Q2 stayed below 20%.
Concentration in Viatris, Aerotex and Atorvastatin+Ezetimibe CDMO programmes. Clarithromycin depends on pending site variation approval. Viatris technology cannot be sold to other customers.
Receivables rose from ₹168 crore to about ₹234 crore; the 75-day realisation cycle and the expected Q3 reduction need checking.
Samba EU-GMP/PIC/S approval timing (FY28) and the ANVISA inspection (Q4 FY27) are open regulatory items.
Undisclosed items: constant-currency growth, detailed capex and asset turns, and the Viatris/Aerotex deal economics were deferred to separate sharing.
Synthimed stake monetisation depends on IndiaRF's sale timing and valuation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line and margin momentum, with specific guidance for CDMO ramp-up and the ₹1,500 crore FY30 vision. Noticeably evasive on FY28 numbers, constant-currency figures, detailed capex and the March 2028 revenue question, deferring these to later calls or separate sharing.

We are in active discussions with two other customers and hope to conclude discussions in the last quarter.
The primary task is execution, to manufacture and deliver.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth above 50% (H1 up 35.8%, Q2 up 50.2%) and a ₹1,500+ crore FY30 target, backed partly by CDMO orders (Ibuprofen ₹20 crore in Q3, ₹20-25 crore in Q4) and ₹250 crore growth capex, but no specific FY27 rupee target or capacity-add timing was given and capex detail was deferred to ConfideLeap.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is 70-75% at both Samba and Derabassi, with ₹250 crore growth capex on track, but no new capacity commissioning date was given beyond the Derabassi warehouse shift in 10-12 months that frees space for manufacturing.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The 20% full-year EBITDA margin needs above 20% in H2 after H1 at 17.97%, and Q1 and Q2 stayed below 20%; concentration in Viatris, Aerotex and Atorvastatin+Ezetimibe CDMO programmes adds execution risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Clarithromycin dry suspension awaits customer variation approval, and Macrogol sachet is supplied; 100-150 of over 330 expected FY27 registrations are already secured, but management said no new molecule is expected in FY28.

rows.label: New-customer revenue of ₹80-90 crore this year
rows.why: Newly acquired international customers are expected to add about ₹80-90 crore of revenue this year, with CDMO incremental revenue of ₹100-130 crore guided for FY27.

rows.label: Samba ANVISA visit and PIC/S/EU approval
rows.why: The ANVISA visit is expected probably in Q4 FY27 and PIC/S/EU approval sometime in FY28, with the ₹45 crore EU-GMP upgrade on schedule, but both are open regulatory items.

rows.label: Synthimed stake monetisation
rows.why: Majority holder IndiaRF may sell some stake in coming quarters, and management sees ₹7,000-8,000 crore value for Synthimed against Ind-Swift's 7.80% holding, with tag-along rights, but timing and valuation are not set.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY27 revenue growth above 50%, the CDMO ramp and the ₹1,500 crore FY30 vision, but evasive on FY28 numbers, the March 2028 ₹1,200-1,250 crore question, constant-currency figures and detailed capex, deferring them to later calls.
